methods.label: K-Means (recommended)
methods.desc: Groups customers into 4 clusters by their orders, spend and recency. Best balance of clear separation and useful business groups.
ins: Regular: the biggest group (70% of customers). Offer loyalty points and personalized discounts.
Regular: 3,054 customers bring 47% of all revenue. Look after them first.
At-Risk: last order about 8 months ago on average. Send win-back emails and special discount offers.

methods.label: K-Means on log scale
methods.desc: Same method after a log transform, so a few huge spenders matter less. Groups are more evenly sized but overlap more.
ins: At-Risk: the biggest group (37% of customers). Send win-back emails and special discount offers.
Champions: 713 customers bring 65% of all revenue. Look after them first.
At-Risk: last order about 6 months ago on average. Send win-back emails and special discount offers.

methods.label: Gaussian Mixture (GMM)
methods.desc: Finds 3 overlapping groups using probabilities. Simple and clear, but fewer segments to act on.
ins: Regular: the biggest group (65% of customers). Offer loyalty points and personalized discounts.
Champions: 337 customers bring 54% of all revenue. Look after them first.
At-Risk: last order about 8 months ago on average. Send win-back emails and special discount offers.

methods.label: DBSCAN
methods.desc: Finds one big core group and flags unusual customers as outliers. Good for spotting special accounts, not for everyday marketing.
ins: Core: the biggest group (97% of customers). Treat as the main audience: regular newsletters and seasonal offers.
Core: 4,225 customers bring 60% of all revenue. Look after them first.
